q-128636.name: Question 3
q-128636.worked_solution:
We distribute the conjunction over the disjunction, as follows:

$$
X∧(Q∨¬Z)≡(X∧Q)∨(X∧¬Z)
$$

Now, since $X∧Q≡Q∧X$ and $X∧¬Z≡¬Z∧X,$ we can write

$$
(X∧Q)∨(X∧¬Z)≡(Q∧X)∨(¬Z∧X).

Which statement is equivalent to X∧(Q∨¬Z)?

a
(Q∧X)∨(¬Z∧X)
b
(¬Z∧Q)∨(¬Z∧X)
c
(Q∧X)∧(¬Z∧X)
d
X∨(Q∧¬Z)
e
¬Z∧(X∨Q)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We distribute the conjunction over the disjunction, as follows:

X∧(Q∨¬Z)≡(X∧Q)∨(X∧¬Z)

Now, since X∧Q≡Q∧X and X∧¬Z≡¬Z∧X, we can write

(X∧Q)∨(X∧¬Z)≡(Q∧X)∨(¬Z∧X).

q-81610.name: Question 7
q-81610.worked_solution:
We distribute the disjunction over the conjunction, as follows:

$$
(¬P∧Q)∨R≡(¬P∨R)∧(Q∨R)
$$

Now, since $¬P∨R≡R∨¬P$ and $Q∨R≡R∨Q$ we can write

$$
(¬P∨R)∧(Q∨R)≡(R∨¬P)∧(R∨Q).
$$

Question 7
?

Which statement is equivalent to (¬P∧Q)∨R?

a
(R∨¬P)∧(R∨Q)
b
(R∨¬P)∧Q
c
(R∨P)∧(¬Q∨R)
d
¬P∧(R∨Q)
e
(R∨¬P)∨(R∨P)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We distribute the disjunction over the conjunction, as follows:

(¬P∧Q)∨R≡(¬P∨R)∧(Q∨R)

Now, since ¬P∨R≡R∨¬P and Q∨R≡R∨Q we can write (¬P∨R)∧(Q∨R)≡(R∨¬P)∧(R∨Q).
